job.title: Software Development Engineer, Selling Partner Trust
job.pay_full: $143,700 – $194,400 a year base salary (Tempe), plus sign-on payments and restricted stock units

details.about: The Selling Partner Trust team protects Amazon's buyers, brand owners and sellers from bad actors, abuse and fraud. It aims to cut false-positive enforcement against seller accounts and listings, and is building a numeric score for seller account health that automatically enforces against bad actors, with a transparent, data-driven process and a clear path forward.
duties: Conceptualize, design, build, test and own software systems
Build services that handle millions of requests a day with millisecond response times and strict SLAs
Deliver automation and experiences using big data sets and distributed frameworks
Help drive the team's technical direction
needs: 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
3+ years of non-internship design or architecture of new and existing systems (design patterns, reliability and scaling)
1+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience
1+ years designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software using C#, C++, Java or Perl
Experience programming with at least one software programming language
nice: 3+ years of the full software development life cycle: coding standards, code reviews, source control, build processes, testing and operations
Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent
details.benefits: Base salary $143,700 – $194,400 a year (Tempe). The package includes sign-on payments and restricted stock units (RSUs); final pay depends on experience, qualifications and location. Benefits include medical, dental, vision and prescription cover, basic life and AD&D insurance with supplemental life options, EAP, mental health support, a medical advice line, flexible spending accounts, adoption and surrogacy reimbursement, 401(k) matching, paid time off and parental leave.
notes: Amazon offers workplace accommodations during the hiring process for candidates with disabilities
